limitations: the application-side behaviour of an exporter against a stopped, slow or rejecting store belongs to #1779 and #1780; what this check proves is that no service of the deployment depends on the pair, which is the startup half of the same rule

the byte bound of the default mode is each store's own free-space guard plus its retention window, not a filesystem quota: a quota needs a quota-enabled filesystem and the quota tools, which an operator opts into

on the pinned victoria-traces, /select/tempo/api/search answers 200 with an empty result for spans the same store serves by id and through the Jaeger API, and /select/tempo/api/traceql/search is not implemented at all; the check therefore proves retrievability by id and by service rather than the search box, and whoever reviews the tier should confirm which search mode the provisioned tempo datasource ends up using

Grafana's own render of the two provisioned datasources is not automated here; the check pins the plugin versions and asserts the datasource definitions and the store APIs behind them, and a reviewer with the tier up should open Explore once per datasource
the OTLP payload is written against the published wire format rather than through the OpenTelemetry SDK on purpose: the question is what the store accepts, and #1779 owns the SDK pins
the live half starts the stores of the committed file, not the whole stack: an end-to-end run with a real instrumented application is #1779 and the matched measurement is #1777/#1780

requests go through the busybox client of a container of this check's own on mrmap-internal rather than a socket from this host, because the deployment publishes no port for either store; that also means the check works against a remote or rootless Docker host, and what it cannot see is a client outside the network being refused - which the offline port check asserts instead
